title: Nobody believed it.
description:
Free storage Gmail offered at launch, roughly 250 to 500 times what rivals gave.

Nobody believed it. Google's founders had a tradition of outlandish April Fools' jokes, and a gigabyte of email sounded preposterous.

Launch capacity was 10,000 users on 300 old machines. Per the AP report, that exclusivity drove demand for invitations.

Google opened it to everyone in 2007. For years, the only way in was to be invited.

Led the project, internally codenamed Caribou.

The date was the joke. The gigabyte was not.

Sources:
- https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/20-years-ago-people-thought-googles-gmail-launch-was-an-april-fools-day-joke - established 1GB of free storage at launch, described as 250 to 500 times the space rivals offered, that the date and Google's prank tradition made people doubt it, invite-only exclusivity, the Caribou codename, Paul Buchheit leading the project, and opening to all in 2007.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gmail - corroborated the 1 April 2004 announcement, the 1GB offer, Paul Buchheit as creator and the Caribou codename.
